instruction: The SQLite database 'Database for tasks.sqlite3' in the current directory has tables: CATEGORY(WARE, CLASS) - which category (CLASS) a ware belongs to (a ware may belong to several categories); MANUFACTURER(BILL_ID, COMPANY) - bills of materials and the companies owning them; MATERIAL(BILL_ID, WARE, AMOUNT) - materials used by a bill; PRODUCT(BILL_ID, WARE, AMOUNT, PRICE) - wares produced by a bill, with amount and price. A bill may produce several wares. For each product show all the unique sets of materials used in different variants of bills of materials producing it, and all the possible byproducts (i.e. additional products in the same bills of materials). There must be exactly one row per ware. Write one row per line as ware;sets;byproducts. Each material set is written as (M1,M2) with values sorted alphabetically and separated with comma (no spaces); the unique sets are sorted alphabetically as strings and joined with |. For a bill without materials the set is (). The byproducts are a comma-separated list (no spaces) of unique wares sorted alphabetically, or an empty string if there are none. Sort rows by ware name. Compute the answer with bash (sqlite3 and/or python3). Work only inside the current directory. When you are done, write ONLY the final answer to the file answer.txt in the current directory (for example with bash: echo 42 > answer.txt).
